newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mutual fund investors optimistic - poll.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mutual fund investors optimistic - poll.

text.p: A third of all U.S. mutual fund investors believe stocks will continue to make headway over the next six months while less than a quarter predict the market will suffer a serious plunge in any of the next 10 years, according to a survey released Wednesday.

Thirty-two percent of mutual fund investors believe stocks will rise during the next six months, 50 percent believe the market will remain the same and only 15 percent predict equities will fall, according to the Liberty Financial Co Inc poll.

Forty-one percent think the market will not suffer a drop of more than 10 percent in total returns in any of the next 10 years. Only 18 percent think stocks could drop more than 20 percent in any of those years and just five percent believe the market may fall more than 30 percent, Liberty said.

The survey indicated fund investors may be overly optimistic about future returns; however most remain long-term investors and said they would not panic over a major market correction, said Porter Morgan, investment strategist with Liberty.
"Very, very few of them really seem to be really looking for what we would call a long, deep bear market such as we had in the past," Morgan told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Only fourteen percent believe the market will fail to match the strong 14 percent annual return stocks have achieved over the last 10 years. Twenty-nine percent believe stocks will outperform over the next 10 years while 56 percent believe the market will match the 14 percent gain.
Since the end of World War II, the market has gained just over 12 percent a year on average, Morgan said.
"They seem to think the future will be as good as one of the best 10-year periods in the past," he said.
But if the market did suffer a serious drop of 20 percent or more, two-thirds to 85 percent of investors said they would hold their funds, while some would add to their positions.
Most investors feel their mutual funds would perform better with Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole in the White House and with a Republican-controlled Congress, the poll found.
Fifty-one percent said the market would climb further under Dole, versus 39 percent who said stocks would perform better if President Clinton was reelected.
Fifty-eight percent thought a Republican Congress would be better for stocks versus 34 percent who believed the Democrats would be better for the market.

The survey of 1,014 investors nationwide, conducted by Louis Harris and Associates in late August and early September, sampled people who bought mutual funds outside an employer-sponsored plan. The survey has a sampling error of plus or minus three percent.
